extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, reporting-guideline developers, bibliometricians and network analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Protocol for a cross-sectional bibliometric and network analysis mapping completed reporting guidelines indexed in the EQUATOR Network Library, describing eligibility, search, extraction, cleaning, analysis and dissemination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a reporting guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘A reporting guideline is a checklist, flow diagram or explicit text to guide authors in reporting a specific type of research, developed using explicit methodology’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only papers meeting this definition will be considered; this is the primary conceptual eligibility standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: included item types and language
rubrics_metrics.description: Include published papers of reporting guidelines (ie, ‘completed’ reporting guidelines) written in English with no restrictions by study design, medical specialty, disease or condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations of existing reporting guidelines in non-English languages will be excluded (eg, CONSORT translation into Spanish or Chinese).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: item types not eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting abstracts, proceedings papers (journals, book based), editorials, book chapters, corrections, retracted publications and other items (eg, data paper, news and notes) will be excluded. Reporting guidelines under development will be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion set ensures the study focuses on completed, peer-reviewed guideline papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope and time-window
rubrics_metrics.description: Search completed reporting guidelines indexed in the EQUATOR Network Library from inception to 31 July 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended date for complementary searches in PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science is 15 April 2019; the EQUATOR library will be used as the primary sampling frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search sources and complementary hand-searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all published papers catalogued in the EQUATOR Network Library and use standard identifiers to search PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science; perform complementary hand-searches of guideline developer websites and contact the EQUATOR Network Library team if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of websites for complementary hand-searches are provided (CONSORT, PRISMA, ARRIVE, STROBE, etc.). Results will be imported into a Microsoft Access database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and selection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: All titles and abstracts will be screened against eligibility criteria by one researcher and verified by a second researcher; full text will be retrieved for unclear items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any discrepancies will be resolved via discussions by the research team, including adjudication by a third researcher if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items to extract
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract title, publication year, journal, subject category, keywords, citations (number of times cited), source, language, document type, authors’ names, authors’ affiliated institution (name, department, address including city), and country, plus standard identifiers (eg, PubMed ID, DOI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw data will be exported from the Web of Science into Microsoft Access for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data export and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data from each paper will be exported (downloaded online) from the Web of Science by one researcher and verified by a second researcher to minimise potential omissions or information errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any discrepancies in extracted data will be resolved via discussion or adjudication by a third researcher if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data cleaning and normalisation of names and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize different forms of an author’s name using coincidence in that author's affiliated institution as the basic criterion; distinguish between institution name components (eg, ‘The Ottawa Hospital’ vs ‘University of Ottawa’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record all variations of macroinstitution names where identifiable; correct typographical, transcription and/or indexing errors; substitute missing data (eg, missing country) via manual web search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keywords (‘author keywords’ and ‘keyword plus’) automatically assigned by the Web of Science to represent conceptual content of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords will be used for topical analyses and visualisations (eg, most frequently used keywords by journal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis: paper-level primary analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analysis of production, citations and collaboration patterns will be based on single papers (paper-level analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive summaries will be produced for authors, institutions, countries and journals (eg, total number of papers and total citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for most-prolific lists and clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the most prolific authors (5 or more published papers), institutions (5 or more papers), countries (10 or more papers), journals (10 or more papers) and the most cited papers (‘top 50 citation classics’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These a priori numeric thresholds define which entities will be highlighted in tables and network cluster identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration pattern metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe collaboration patterns with: number of signatures (total number of authors included in all the papers of each author), number of collaborators, number of papers with coauthors, collaborations between authors (‘interindividual collaboration’), collaboration index (mean number of signatories per paper), interinstitutional collaboration and international collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For institutions differentiate domestic interinstitutional collaboration (same country) vs international interinstitutional collaboration (different countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Network construction and visualization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct collaboration networks for authors, institutions and countries and present network diagrams as undirected-weighted graphs where node sizes are proportional to the number of papers, links are bidirectional, and link thicknesses are proportional to the number of collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify clusters of more intense collaboration by applying a priori thresholds (‘collaboration intensity’) based on numbers of papers signed in collaboration between authors (5+), institutions (5+), and countries (10+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality measures and their interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate key standard measures and metrics for quantifying network structure: degree of centrality, closeness and betweenness. Degree counts connected links; closeness measures mean distance from a node to other nodes; betweenness measures extent a node lies on paths between other nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these measures to identify prominent ('key') members of the scientific community and to characterise network shape and information flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical (textual/semantic) analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct topical (linguistic, semantic or textual) data analyses to determine topic coverage: identify most frequently used keywords and present word clouds and co-words networks representing co-occurrence of highly frequent words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word clouds will depict term frequency graphically (larger words = higher frequency); co-word networks show co-occurrence relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple publications of identical guideline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary (guideline-level) analysis will integrate data for multiple (identical) papers of a single reporting guideline by counting authorship and collaboration data once and computing citation impact by grouping total citations across multiple identical papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses simultaneous or duplicate publications aimed at wider dissemination (eg, CONSORT, PRISMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup (pre/post) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake subgroup analysis comparing papers and guidelines before 2008 (pre-EQUATOR Network) versus after 2008 (post-EQUATOR Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compares productivity, citation and collaboration patterns relative to the EQUATOR Network launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses for collaboration thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on productivity and collaboration patterns, explore sensitivity analyses related to thresholds (‘collaboration intensity’) using different numbers of papers in collaboration (eg, between authors, institutions and countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stability of results across alternative threshold settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and visualization tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce relational structure (network) visualisations and metrics using PAJEK; draw word clouds using Wordle; explore additional visualization tools as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAJEK is cited as a free software package for large network analyses; Wordle is used for graphical word-frequency representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise data as frequencies and percentages for categorical variables or median and IQR for continuous variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the basic quantitative summary approach for extracted bibliometric variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and dissemination commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: All data underlying the findings will be deposited in a cross-disciplinary public repository (eg, Open Science Framework or Zenodo) and findings will be published in peer-reviewed journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendments to the protocol will be outlined and reported in the final manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public involvement statement
rubrics_metrics.description: No patients and/or public were involved in setting the research question, developing the plans, advising on interpretation or writing up results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no plans to disseminate the results specifically to the patient community; this is an explicit non-involvement declaration.
